true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
New downsize overload silently shadows the 4-argument downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height)

`def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (line 149) redefines the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` method declared at line 145; in Ruby the later definition wins, so the 4-argument form is unreachable. Any caller passing explicit dimensions (e.g. `OptimizedImage.downsize(src, dst, 1024, 768)`) is now dispatched to the new method with `dimensions = 1024` and `opts = 768`; `optimize` then evaluates `opts[:allow_animation]` and raises `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for 768:Integer` instead of producing a `1024x768` instruction. Even when no exception is raised, `dimensions` is a bare Integer, yielding a broken `-resize` argument. Callers elsewhere in the codebase or scripts that use the width/height form will break silently. Remove the four-argument overload or give the string-dimensions entry point a distinct name.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client upload limit hard-coded to 10MB, ignoring max_image_size_kb/max_attachment_size_kb site settings

`validateUploadedFile` previously derived the limit from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`; it now always uses `10 * 1024` KB for both images and attachments. Attachments are not auto-downsized on the server, so sites configured with a smaller `max_attachment_size_kb` will now accept up to 10MB in the browser and only fail later with a less clear server error (or the setting is effectively bypassed). The same applies to images where an admin deliberately configured a limit below 10MB. In addition, the 413 handler at line 246 now reports `max_size_kb: 10MB` regardless of the web server's real limit, so the error message can be wrong. The limit should stay driven by the site settings (or a dedicated setting for the resize threshold).

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
Downsize loop with at most five 80% steps cannot bring files more than ~3x the limit under the limit

Repeatedly applying `-resize 80%` five times yields only 0.8^5 ≈ 0.33 of the original, so a file more than roughly 3x `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` is still oversized after the loop and `Upload.create_for` then rejects it. The advertised feature (accept large images by shrinking them) therefore still fails for genuinely large uploads, e.g. a 10MB image on a 1MB limit. Each pass is also a separate lossy re-encode (no `-quality` specified), so intermediate steps degrade the image more than necessary. The required scale factor should be computed from `tempfile.size / limit` (or the loop should recompute a percentage from the current size) rather than using fixed 80% steps.

Downsizing an animated GIF keeps only the first frame when allow_animated_thumbnails is off

The controller's new resize path calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. When that setting is false (the default), `optimize` selects `downsize_instructions`, whose command contains `#{from}[0]`, i.e. only the first frame of a multi-frame GIF. Because the downsized temp file replaces the upload, an animated GIF larger than `max_image_size_kb` is permanently stored as a static single-frame image, silently destroying the user's animation. The animated instruction set is only used when the setting is explicitly enabled. Animated uploads should either always go through the animated/`gifsicle` path or be exempted from automatic downsizing.

No tests for the new automatic downsizing behavior or the OptimizedImage API refactor

The PR adds a multi-iteration in-place resize loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` and changes the public signatures of `OptimizedImage.resize/downsize/optimize`, but no specs were added or updated. Tests covering (a) an oversized image that must be shrunk, (b) a file that remains oversized after five attempts, (c) an animated GIF and an SVG upload, and (d) a call to `downsize` with explicit width/height would have caught the shadowed-method bug and the first-frame truncation. Please add model/controller specs for these paths.

Resize loop runs ImageMagick on SVG uploads, which convert cannot faithfully handle

The guard only checks `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`, and that helper's image list includes SVG, so an SVG larger than `max_image_size_kb` is fed to `OptimizedImage.downsize` → `convert`. `OptimizedImage.create_for` deliberately special-cases `.svg` (it copies the file instead of calling `resize`), showing that `convert` is not suitable for vector files. The result is either a rewritten/rasterized file different from what the user uploaded (data loss) or a failed `convert`; in the failure case the loop still spawns five pointless `convert` processes per upload before giving up. Exclude SVG (and any format that cannot round-trip through `convert`) from the resize loop.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing ids cause 500 instead of a clean not-found response

`update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`. If the id does not exist, `save_host(nil)` calls `nil.host=` and `nil.destroy` raises. A stale admin UI request gets a 500 instead of a clean 404/JSON error. Use `find_by` and return an error when nil.

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Host matching drops the port while validation allows it

Validation explicitly allows an optional `:port`, and `before_validation` keeps it (it only strips the scheme and path). But `record_for_host` matches `URI(referer).host`, which omits the port, against the full stored `host`. A saved host such as `example.com:3000` therefore never matches a referer whose host is `example.com`. Either reject ports in validation or compare `host:port` consistently. The bound lookup value is also not downcased, so a mixed-case referer host can miss a lower-cased row.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration copies old host values raw and interpolates them into SQL

The old `embeddable_hosts` SiteSetting accepted schemes and paths (the removed code parsed them with URI and old specs used `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234`). The migration puts `h` verbatim into the new column via `INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`, bypassing `EmbeddableHost` normalization and also not escaping quotes. Records like `http://eviltrout.com` or `example.com/1234` can never match `record_for_host`'s `URI(referer).host` comparison, so existing embeddings stop working after upgrade; a quote in the old setting also breaks the migration. Normalize and parameterize the insert.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration copies old host values raw and interpolates them into SQL

The old `embeddable_hosts` SiteSetting accepted schemes and paths (the removed code parsed them with URI and old specs used `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234`). The migration puts `h` verbatim into the new column via `INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`, bypassing `EmbeddableHost` normalization and also not escaping quotes. Records like `http://eviltrout.com` or `example.com/1234` can never match `record_for_host`'s `URI(referer).host` comparison, so existing embeddings stop working after upgrade; a quote in the old setting also breaks the migration. Normalize and parameterize the insert.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when embed_category has no matching setting row

The migration runs `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` for the `embed_category` lookup. That setting was optional and `site_settings` only stores rows that were changed, so when it is absent (or blank, so the join matches no category) `execute` returns no rows, `[0]` is nil, and `['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration. The fallback lookup for `uncategorized_category_id` makes the same nil assumption. Use `first`/`find_by` and guard before dereferencing.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

false_positives.candidate:
Admin endpoint specs only assert inheritance

The new admin controller specs contain only a subclass assertion. None of the new create/update/destroy behavior is tested: host normalization, category assignment/fallback, missing ids, destroy, or authorization. These endpoints currently contain 500 paths, and the migration behavior is also untested. Add request specs for the happy path and missing-id/error cases.

Embedded test requests fruit 2 but only ever checks fruit 1

The test now calls `store.find('fruit', 2)`, but the pretender's `/fruits/:id` handler always returns `fruits[0]` (apple, `color_ids: [1,2]`), and the assertions still expect `[1,2]`. The test passes without exercising banana/id 2 (`color_ids: [3]`), so it does not verify id-specific embedded hydration. Update the fixture to return the requested fruit or keep the test on id 1.

Feed imports can lose their configured category after this change

The category for every imported embed is now `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url).try(:category_id)`. Feed polling imports arbitrary feed item URLs through `TopicEmbed.import` without going through `TopicRetriever`'s host check; if the feed host was not also in the old `embeddable_hosts` list, the migration creates no record for it and `category_id` becomes nil. Existing feed-polling installs will start creating uncategorized topics (or fail when uncategorized topics are disabled) instead of using the old `embed_category` setting. Migration/fallback needs to cover the feed-polling host.

Host validation rejects valid TLDs longer than five characters

The regex requires the TLD to be `[a-z]{2,5}`, so valid hostnames such as `example.museum`, `example.travel`, or modern long TLDs cannot be saved as embeddable hosts. Admins cannot configure otherwise valid embedding sources. Use a looser hostname check or rely on URI parsing.

No uniqueness constraint on host makes the category mapping ambiguous

Neither the model nor the migration enforces a unique host (case-insensitively). The admin UI can create two rows for the same host with different categories, and the migration can copy duplicates from the old newline list. `record_for_host` then returns whichever row the database returns first, making the category used for new embedded topics non-deterministic. Add a case-insensitive uniqueness validation and matching unique index.

Plural embedded ids are deleted even when hydration fails

In the new plural branch, `obj[k].map(...)` can return `undefined` entries when the side-loaded collection is absent or partial, but the code still assigns `obj[plural] = hydrated` and deletes the original `*_ids` key. Unlike the singular branch, it never checks whether lookup succeeded. That silently changes the model shape and loses ids for any rest_serializer payload that sends `foo_ids` without all `foo` objects (or without a `foos` collection). Preserve the original ids unless every reference resolves, and don't create arrays of undefined.

UI clears the category after saving with the uncategorized fallback

When saving a host without a selected category, the server assigns `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, but the success handler overwrites `host.category` with `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))`, where `categoryId` is null. The table then shows a blank category until reload even though the host was saved to the uncategorized category. Use the category returned/assigned by the server, or map the null id to the uncategorized category.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsubscribe crashes on missing TopicUser and bypasses TopicUser.change

`TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil whenever a logged-in user visits the unsubscribe URL without an existing topic_users row (for example a direct visit or a stale email link), and the next `tu.notification_level` call raises NoMethodError, returning a 500. Even when the row exists, assigning the level and calling `tu.save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change`, so `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id` are not updated and the `notification_level_change` MessageBus event is not published, leaving the topic's notification reason stale. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)`, which upserts and goes through the normal path.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Explicit render in perform_show_response breaks canonical URL on topic pages

Adding `render :show` inside `perform_show_response` causes the normal `show` action to render before it executes `canonical_url` (line 87). `canonical_url` sets `@canonical_url` for the layout, so topic show pages will no longer emit the canonical link (or will use a stale one). Move the canonical URL assignment before `perform_show_response`, or render explicitly only from `unsubscribe`.

New locale interpolation makes unsubscribe_url mandatory for all add_unsubscribe_link emails

`unsubscribe_link` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder` calls this translation from both `body` and `html_part` whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true, and only UserNotifications was updated to pass the new option. Any other mailer or plugin that uses `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to send email. Provide a fallback to `user_preferences_url` or make the option explicitly required and update all callers.

No coverage for the new unsubscribe behavior

The spec change only adds `unsubscribe_url` to the builder options; it does not assert that the rendered body or HTML actually contains the per-topic unsubscribe URL. There are also no controller/route specs for `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (missing TopicUser, watching/tracking to regular/muted, slug redirect) or for the new Ember route. The nil crash and the notification-level behavior above would pass CI.

State-changing unsubscribe action is a GET without a CSRF/token check

`unsubscribe` changes the current user's notification level in response to a plain GET and is authorized only by the session cookie. A third-party page can therefore embed `/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe` as an image/link and mute a logged-in user's topic (and email link scanners can trigger it too). Use a signed per-user/per-topic token in the emailed URL, or require a POST with the normal CSRF protection.

Unsubscribe only downgrades watching/tracking users to regular

When the user's level is tracking or watching, the action sets it to regular instead of muted. Regular still sends notifications for replies and mentions, so the page text 'You will stop receiving notifications' is false and a mention/reply email can keep arriving after the user clicks the unsubscribe link. Set the level to muted when the intent is to stop notifications, or change the branch and copy to describe a downgrade.

Unsubscribe route name does not match the added template path

The route is declared at top level as `topicUnsubscribe`, so Ember's default template lookup is `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`. The PR adds `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which is the path for a nested route named `topic.unsubscribe`, not for a top-level `topicUnsubscribe` route. As written the new URL has no template and will render blank or throw a template-not-found error. Either nest the route under the `topic` resource as `this.route('unsubscribe', { path: '/unsubscribe' })` or rename the added template to `topic-unsubscribe.hbs`.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Validation triggers a DB write and double-counts blocked-email statistics

`EmailValidator#validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`, and `should_block?` (app/models/blocked_email.rb lines 12-17) loads the matching record, increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, and calls `record.save`. This means a simple `valid?`/`save` check now performs a database write. In `UsersController#create` the user is validated twice on the same request: `user.valid?` (line 168) and then `user.save` (line 172), so a single signup attempt against a blocked (or even `do_nothing`) email increments `match_count` by 2 instead of 1. Match counts will be inflated unpredictably, defeating the purpose of these statistics for spotting spam campaigns, and read-only validation paths unexpectedly mutate the DB. The stat update should be decoupled from the pure predicate and triggered once per real block event (e.g., after a confirmed rejection), not on every validation invocation.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and bypassable

`BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` compares the raw submitted email against the stored string with exact case. E-mail addresses are treated case-insensitively in practice, and nothing downcases the user's email when it is set/validated (`User.new_from_params` stores it verbatim). So an entry for `spam@bad.com` will not block a signup using `Spam@Bad.com` or `spam@BAD.com`, and imported/manually-entered records in mixed case won't match either — trivially bypassing the blocklist. Normalize on both sides: downcase/`Email.downcase` the value in `should_block?` (and ideally normalize the stored `email` in a `before_validation`/`before_save` so the unique index also behaves case-insensitively).

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
New validator spec does not cover the ported domain restrictions or the real lookup

The only new validator specs stub `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, so they neither exercise the actual database lookup/scoping nor verify the end-to-end behavior (`user.valid?` returning false for a blocked email). More importantly, this PR moves the `email_domains_whitelist`/`email_domains_blacklist` logic out of `User#email_validator` into `EmailValidator`, but no spec covers that moved logic (whitelist pass/fail, blacklist pass/fail). A regression in the relocated domain-restriction behavior would go undetected. Add specs covering the whitelist and blacklist branches (and ideally one integration spec that a blocked email makes a `User` invalid), plus a test for the new `errors`/`values` fields returned by `UsersController#create`.

Non-atomic counter update loses matches under concurrency

`should_block?` performs a read-modify-write: `record.match_count += 1; record.save`. Two concurrent requests matching the same blocked email both read count N and write N+1, losing one increment. Since these counters are the signal used to identify spam waves (exactly when many concurrent attempts happen), the undercounting is most severe in the scenario the data is meant to detect. Use an atomic update such as `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(["match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?", Time.zone.now])` (or `increment_counter`) instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Origin check uses substring matching instead of exact origin equality

`if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) return;` accepts any origin that appears as a substring of the trusted URL, for example `http://forum.example` when `discourseUrl` is `http://forum.example.com`, or the same host on a different port. Such a page can send a `discourse-resize` message and control the iframe height. Compare `e.origin` against the normalized origin of `discourseUrl` exactly.

true_positives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage targetOrigin is a full referer URL instead of an origin

The resize script sends `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. `targetOrigin` must be a serialized origin (scheme://host[:port]); a referer with a path (and query string, which ERB also HTML-escapes to `&` inside the script) does not match the parent origin. The browser therefore drops the message, so the iframe never receives the height and content is clipped to the initial iframe size. Build the target origin from `URI(request.referer).scheme`, host, and port (or use a controlled site setting), not the full URL.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Imported feed/readability HTML is stored as raw HTML and rendered without sanitization

`TopicEmbed.import` sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns the raw string for that method, bypassing Markdown/sanitization. `Jobs::PollFeed` feeds arbitrary RSS/Atom content here (after `CGI.unescapeHTML`, which can turn escaped `<script>` into a real script tag), and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19` emits `raw post.cooked`. The readability path only filters tag/attribute names, not dangerous URL schemes, and line 13 interpolates the feed-provided URL unescaped into the raw post. A malicious or compromised feed can therefore inject script/event-handler HTML and execute it in the forum origin when the embed is viewed. Sanitize the HTML (and URL schemes/attributes) before storing it, or do not use the raw_html cook method for untrusted feed content.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Invalid `end if` makes the embed template fail to compile

Line 6 closes the header `if` with `end if` and no condition. ERB compiles this to Ruby containing `end if`, which is a SyntaxError, so every request that renders `embed/best` will raise instead of displaying discussion highlights or the start-discussion link. It should just be `<%- end %>`. Controller specs do not render views by default, so this is not caught.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed items without `content` raise NoMethodError and abort polling

`i.content.scrub` assumes every RSS/Atom item has a `content` field. Many valid feeds provide only `description` or `summary`, so `i.content` is nil and `nil.scrub` raises, aborting the entire poll and preventing all later items from importing. Use `i.content || i.description` (and handle nil) before scrubbing/unescaping.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Guard tests pass without exercising the setting under test

The `feed_polling_url` test stubs only `feed_polling_url` to nil; it leaves `feed_polling_enabled?` at its default false, so `execute` short-circuits before the URL check. The `embed_by_username` test has the same issue. These tests would still pass if the corresponding condition were deleted. Stub all earlier guards true in each test, and only the condition under test false, to make the assertion meaningful.

URL absolutization corrupts protocol-relative URLs and misses path-relative URLs

Only root-relative links are rewritten, and protocol-relative URLs are corrupted: `//cdn.example.com/x` satisfies `start_with?('/')`, then `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, producing `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/x` instead of `http://cdn.example.com/x`. Path-relative URLs such as `foo/bar` are not absolutized at all. The same issue exists for `img[src]` below. Treat `//` separately and resolve relative URLs against the article URI.

Unvalidated `open(url)` allows command execution/file reads from Disqus links

`TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url)` before any URL validation. Ruby's `Kernel#open` treats a string beginning with `|` as a shell command and other strings as local file paths, so a malicious Disqus export can put e.g. `|touch /tmp/pwned` or `/etc/passwd` in a thread link; `lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148` now passes `t[:link]` directly to this method. Running the importer would execute the command or read the file. Validate that the URL is http/https and use an HTTP client (with redirect/size/timeout handling) instead of Kernel#open.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items mixin omits -moz-box-align fallback

The new `align-items()` mixin emits `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-flex-align`, and `align-items`, but omits `-moz-box-align`. Since the new `flexbox()` and `inline-flex()` mixins explicitly fall back to `display: -moz-box`/`display: -moz-inline-box`, old Firefox versions will select the legacy box display but ignore the requested alignment. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment;` for parity; the `-ms-align-items` declaration is not a recognized IE property and can be removed.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

false_positives.candidate:
Flex layout breaks right-aligned small-action button

Adding `@include flexbox()` to `.small-action` changes its children to flex items. The existing `.small-action button { float: right; }` rule (line 309) can no longer right-align a button that is a direct flex child because floats are ignored on flex items. Also, `.small-action-desc` is not given `flex-grow`, so it no longer spans the remaining row width; if the button is nested inside it, the internal float will no longer push the button to the full row’s right edge either. The undo/act action button will therefore sit next to the description instead of at the right side. Add `margin-left: auto` to the button or make `.small-action-desc` grow.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. For forward cursors (`is_prev` false) this changes `queryset[offset:stop]` to `queryset[max(0, offset):...]`, and for `is_prev` it assigns `offset` unchanged. Either reject negative offsets explicitly or document that they are clamped.

The PR adds a new paginator class and a new conditional code path in the audit log endpoint but no tests. Because `OptimizedCursorPaginator` diverges from `BasePaginator`/`DateTimePaginator` in `get_item_key` and `value_from_cursor`, a single test paging an audit-log queryset with `optimized_pagination=true` would have caught the `math.floor(datetime)` crash, the integer-vs-timestamp `WHERE` clause, and the unaccepted `enable_advanced_features` kwarg. `value_from_cursor()` returns `cursor.value` unchanged (an integer/timestamp number). `BasePaginator.build_queryset()` then interpolates that value into a raw `WHERE` clause on the ordered column (`... WHERE audit_log_entry.datetime <= %s`). For audit logs the column is a timestamp, so comparing it to an integer either raises a Postgres "operator does not exist: timestamp with time zone <= bigint" error or produces wrong ordering. `DateTimePaginator` deliberately overrides this method to convert the cursor value back with `datetime.fromtimestamp(value / multiplier)`; the optimized paginator must do the same (or reuse `DateTimePaginator`) for datetime-ordered querysets. The endpoint chooses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` vs `DateTimePaginator` from the client-supplied `optimized_pagination=true` query param, but the two paginators encode the cursor `value` differently: `DateTimePaginator` uses millisecond epoch values and converts them back with `datetime.fromtimestamp`, while `OptimizedCursorPaginator` stores/interprets the raw field value. `self.paginate(...)` is `Endpoint.paginate`, whose signature is `(request, queryset, order_by, paginator_cls, on_results, default_per_page, max_per_page, max_hits, count_hits, known_hits, cursor)`. false_positives.candidate:
Changing span buffer keys from sets to sorted sets breaks existing Redis data during rollout

Span buffers are stored at `span-buf:s:{project:trace}:span_id`. Before this change those keys are Redis sets; this diff starts writing them with `ZADD` and later calls `ZCARD`/`ZSCAN`/`ZUNIONSTORE` (`buffer.py` lines 197 and 434, plus `add-buffer.lua`). During a rolling deploy, any old set key touched by the new consumer, or any old consumer touching a new zset key, will get a `WRONGTYPE` error. Existing keys have a TTL up to `redis_ttl` (default 3600 seconds), so affected batches can fail and spans/segments can be lost or stuck until keys expire. There is no dual read/write path, versioned key prefix, or migration/flush step.

New OptimizedCursorPaginator and audit-log branch have no tests

`OptimizedCursorPaginator` is a new ~90-line paginator used by the audit-log endpoint, but no test instantiates it or calls the endpoint with `optimized_pagination=true`. Basic coverage would have caught both the datetime `TypeError` and the negative-offset `ValueError`. Add tests for first/next/prev pages, forged negative offsets, and the audit-log optimized path.

No test exercises the new ZPOPMIN eviction path

All buffer tests still use only a handful of spans, so the new >1000-span eviction path is completely untested. There is no coverage for the cap being enforced, eviction ordering by `end_timestamp_precise`, retention of a root/segment span, or cleanup/redirect behavior for evicted spans. A regression here silently drops span data, so a test with more than 1000 spans should verify the resulting segment contents and Redis key cleanup.

Redirect-chain traversal limit reduced from 10,000 to 1,000

The loop that resolves parent redirects was changed from `for i = 0, 10000` to `for i = 0, 1000`, removing the comment that documented the old limit. If a trace's span-buffer redirect chain is deeper than 1000, the loop stops at an intermediate span id, so the current span is attached to the wrong buffer and segments can be split or duplicated. This is an abrupt behavior change unrelated to the eviction work and has no test; either restore the old bound or justify and test the new one.

Span buffer hard-codes 1000-span cap and ignores SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans

Eviction is now `if span_count > 1000 then zpopmin(...)` inside the Lua script, while the Python span-count check was removed from `_load_segment_data`. `SpansBuffer` still exposes `max_segment_spans` (default 1001) and passes nothing to the script, so any configured value is silently ignored and the actual limit is always 1000, which is also one lower than the default. Operators/tests cannot tune the cap, and the Python span-count safety check no longer matches the Lua behavior.

ZUNIONSTORE sums duplicate timestamp scores instead of preserving the latest

The script uses `zunionstore set_key, 2, set_key, span_key` (and the same for `parent_key`) without an `AGGREGATE` option. Redis's default is `SUM`, so if a span payload is present in both source sets its score becomes the sum of two `end_timestamp_precise` values rather than the max/latest timestamp. This occurs routinely with at-least-once duplicate/reprocessed spans: a duplicate child is re-added under its parent key and then merged into the destination where the first copy already exists. Since `ZPOPMIN` later uses the score to decide which spans to evict, duplicated spans can be moved to the wrong end of the ordering and be kept or evicted incorrectly. This PR adds a gitlink entry at the repository root named `sentry-repo`, pointing at the base commit. Cache key uses Python hash and can collide across project sets

The eligibility cache key is `error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))}`. Different project sets can produce the same Python hash, so a cached allowlist result for one set can be reused for another set in the same organization, causing `upsampled_count()` to run for non-allowlisted projects and inflating counts. Use the serialized sorted project IDs (or a cryptographic digest) as the key instead.

Discover eligibility uses a naive substring of request.GET instead of the actual query

`_is_error_focused_query` returns True for any raw request query containing `event.type:error`, so it also matches negated or mixed queries such as `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. It also ignores the actual `query` argument passed to `_get_event_stats`; dashboard split calls with derived `errors_only_query`/`transactions_only_query` are judged against the original request query instead. This can apply `upsampled_count()` to transaction rows where `sample_weight` is absent, or skip upsampling for an error-only derived query, producing incorrect counts.

Internal upsampled_count function is exposed to user queries

The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction does not set `private=True`, unlike neighboring internal functions such as `count_if`. User-supplied queries can therefore request `yAxis=upsampled_count()` directly, bypassing the allowlist/dataset/query checks in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and obtaining sample-weighted counts for arbitrary projects. Mark it private if it is only intended to be emitted internally.

`self.request` is a `rest_framework.request.Request`, whose `GET` attribute is a read-only property. `self.request.GET = QueryDict("")` and the later assignments at lines 79, 83, 87, 97, and 100 raise `AttributeError: can't set attribute`, so the new helper tests never run. Build the query string through `RequestFactory().get("/", data=...)` or set the underlying `_request.GET` instead.

Only `timeseries_columns` is transformed to `upsampled_count()`; `orderby=self.get_orderby(request)` and `equations=self.get_equation_list(...)` still use raw `count()`. The endpoint can route a discover query through the metrics layer via `use_metrics_layer` (line 311), but `upsampled_count` was only registered in `DiscoverDataset`. The transform at line 296 is applied based solely on dataset/request and does not check `forceMetricsLayer` or the `organizations:use-metrics-layer` feature, so in that configuration the generated metrics-layer query can reference an unknown `upsampled_count()` function. Gate the transform on the metrics-layer setting or register the function there.

The new backup-code input is a plain `TextField` with no `autoCapitalize="none"`/`autoCorrect="off"`/`spellCheck={false}`. Codes are generated as lowercase hex (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`) and the server-side match is an exact, case-sensitive `array.indexOf(value)` after only stripping `-` (`next-auth-options.ts:144` and `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:61`). true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so a code can be used twice or resurrected

The new backup-code login branch decrypts `user.backupCodes` into an array, nulls the matched entry (`backupCodes[index] = null`) and then writes the whole re-encrypted array back with `prisma.user.update`. This is a read-modify-write with no transaction or conditional update. Two login requests that arrive concurrently with the same code both match it and both return success, so the "each backup code can be used exactly once" guarantee advertised in `backup_code_instructions` is not enforced. Worse, two concurrent requests with *different* codes each write back a list derived from the same original snapshot, so the last write wins and the code consumed by the other request is silently restored and becomes reusable. Because an attacker typically does not need parallelism, this is not trivially exploitable, but the single-use property of a security credential must hold under concurrency. Suggested fix: perform the removal atomically (e.g. a `updateMany` guarded on the exact previous encrypted value, or a transaction with a row lock / `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`), or store codes as individual rows and delete by id/`deleteMany`.

New `required` on the password field blocks disabling 2FA for accounts with no password

`required` was added to the password `PasswordField`. The field is rendered whenever the caller doesn't pass `disablePassword` (the default), and the API deliberately treats the password as optional: `disable.ts` only verifies it `if (user.password && user.identityProvider === IdentityProvider.CAL)`. Accounts that have 2FA enabled but no password (e.g. a user who set up 2FA while using CAL credentials and later signed in with Google, which nulls `password`, or SAML/Google accounts with 2FA) can legitimately disable 2FA server-side, but the browser now refuses to submit the form with an empty required field, so they are blocked in the UI. The client-side constraint should mirror the server rule (e.g. only mark it required when the account actually has a password).

No test covers logging in with a backup code or its single-use behaviour

The PR's core security behaviours are untested. The added assertions only verify that the download produces a file named `cal-backup-codes.txt`, that the copy button shows a toast, and that Close works (`// TODO: check file content`, `// TODO: check clipboard content`), and a `// TODO: add more backup code tests` is left behind. Nothing exercises: logging in via "Lost access" with a real code, rejection of a wrong code, the fact that a consumed code cannot be reused (the guarantee the UI copy makes), or disabling 2FA with a backup code. Since the consumption logic lives in `next-auth-options.ts` and is exactly the part that can silently regress (including the concurrency issue above), at least a happy-path login-with-backup-code test and a reuse-rejection test should be added before merge.

Third-party identity-provider guard makes backup codes unusable for OAuth accounts with 2FA

The existing guard `if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode) throw new Error(ErrorCode.ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled)` runs before the new backup-code branch. A user with a GOOGLE/SAML identity provider who has 2FA enabled necessarily submits a backup code with an empty `totpCode`, so they always hit this error and can never use their backup codes, even though `loginWithTotp` routes such users through the 2FA login page. Either the guard should also accept a supplied `backupCode`, or the limitation should be made explicit (and the UI should not offer a path that can never succeed) — as written, the feature silently does not apply to that group of 2FA users.

missing_backup_codes message tells users to generate codes in settings, which is impossible

The new `missing_backup_codes` string reads "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." but no such setting exists: backup codes are only produced by `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup`, which returns `TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled` for any user who already has 2FA on, and there is no UI to regenerate them. Every user who enabled 2FA before this migration (`backupCodes` is `NULL`) and then clicks "Lost access" will follow the advice, find nothing, and be stuck. Either provide a regenerate-codes entry point in the 2FA settings section or change the text to describe what the user can actually do (e.g. disable and re-enable 2FA).

onEnable is only fired from the backup-codes Close button, so dismissing the dialog otherwise leaves 2FA state stale

Before this change `onEnable()` was called as soon as the enable API returned 200. Now enablement is only reported to the parent from the `backup-codes-close` button (`resetState(); onEnable();`). The dialog is controlled by the parent and Radix closes it on Escape (and on other dismissal paths) via `onOpenChange`, none of which call `onEnable` or `resetState`. Consequence: a user who enables 2FA and closes the dialog with Escape gets a server state where 2FA is enabled, while the settings page still shows the toggle as unchecked; if they retry, `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup` answers `TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled` and they get a generic "something went wrong" error. The internal `step` also stays on `DisplayBackupCodes`, so re-opening the modal later shows the old backup-code screen instead of the password step. `onEnable` should be invoked (and state reset) whenever the dialog is dismissed after a successful enable, not only from one button.
